newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up again led by brewery sector.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up again led by brewery sector.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Thursday for the second successive day led by strong gains in the brewery sector, brokers said.
They added the market was likely to continue its bull run Friday, but warned some stocks might see profit-taking after the recent rises.
Thursday, the General Index rose 1.58 percent to 1,613.7 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 1.60 percent to 2,152.8 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
Strong rumors that Compaa Nacional de Cerveza and the country's largest brewery Backus y Johnston were set to merge propelled the sector, brokers said..
Compaa Nacional de Cerveza closed up 10.14 percent at 1.52 soles in heavy volume of 4.76 million shares.
Backus also received a boost on the rumors as the stock's price ended up 2.46 percent at 2.92 soles on 1.78 million shares.
"The speculation on the possible merger of the breweries caused the increase in their prices and this had a knock-on effect throughout the market," said Lorenzo Wong of local brokerage Intercapital.
A source at Grupo Backus, which owns both breweries, told Reuters after trading ended that the group was considering merging the two companies in an effort to increase production.
Among other leaders, benchmark Telefnica del Per climbed 1.43 percent to 5.69 soles in volume of 1.58 million shares.
But Tele 2000 continued to underperform compared to the market's general trend. The telecom dropped 2.41 percent to 4.05 soles in meager volume of 11,300 shares.
In a total of 2,818 trades, 50 stocks rose, 22 fell and 32 were stable. Volume was a healthy 56.5 million ($22.5 million).
